empty.noProject: Open a work to use the console.

nonfiction.title: Deterministic views only
nonfiction.body: For non-fiction, NVS reads your transcript directly — Cast shows who speaks and how much (by character volume), and Timeline shows the flow. AI analysis is off for now; custom extraction will arrive as a skill you can run on demand.

health.noAi: No AI connected — steps will be skipped until you add one.

tip.viewing: Viewing a past version — return to current to update
tip.cycle: Timeline has a leads_to cycle — fix it so the analysis can walk the graph
tip.dirty: Read changed scenes into the analysis
tip.graph: The timeline graph changed since the last run — re-run to update
tip.skim_one: {{count}} scene read fast — run an Expert pass to build character arcs & profiles
tip.skim_other: {{count}} scenes read fast — run an Expert pass to build character arcs & profiles

coherence.tipViewing: Viewing a past version — return to current to check
coherence.tipNone: No characters with both a page and an arc yet
coherence.tipReady: Diff each character’s page against what the story shows

readiness.tip: Ask the AI to preflight-check the project before an analysis run
readiness.label: Readiness check

rebuild.confirmBody: Rebuilds the analysis cleanly from your scenes when it's drifted out of sync with your story. Your writing is never touched.

table.whenBody: threads, arcs or coherence look wrong — usually after renaming or restructuring chapters
table.whatBody: clears the derived analysis (threads, arcs, coherence, version history) and re-reads your files
table.writingBody: never touched — only the analysis is rebuilt
table.safetyBody: the current analysis is backed up to a .nvs.bak-… folder first, so nothing is lost
table.afterBody: re-run the AI passes to refill threads/arcs/coherence

reanalyze.confirmBody_one: This re-reads {{count}} scene even though they're up to date — about {{count}} AI call via {{conn}} (handy after switching models). The database is snapshotted first.
reanalyze.confirmBody_other: This re-reads {{count}} scenes even though they're up to date — about {{count}} AI calls via {{conn}} (handy after switching models). The database is snapshotted first.
reanalyze.selectedTip: Re-read the selected scenes even though they're up to date (e.g. on a faster model)

recent.title: Recent updates
recent.historyTip: See what each past run analyzed, by chapter
recent.empty: Past updates will appear here once you run one.
recent.prunedTip: Older versions are pruned to save space — this one can no longer be previewed or restored
recent.restoreTip: Make this the current version (reversible — your current version stays in the list)

provenance.versionPrunedTip: Snapshot pruned — too old to preview (only the newest versions are kept)

coherenceRow.behind: Coherence is behind — re-check this version
coherenceRow.tip: Coherence check (based on this analysis version)

scenes.empty: No scenes yet — write one, and it'll show up here.

db.healthTip: Check DB health — the agent audits duplicates, residue, orphans & staleness (read-only; you confirm any fix)
db.none: No database yet — run analysis to build it.

connections.intro: Provider keys — only one is active at a time (like saved cards). The active connection drives both chat (right-hand panel) and analysis passes.
connections.label: Label
connections.keyless: No API key — runs on your Claude Code login. Log in once with claude if you haven't.

notice.keySaved: Key saved — set it active and test it in chat.

mcp.title: In-app MCP server
mcp.intro: An agent (Claude Code / Desktop) connects to the running app and calls these as live tools — the same engine contract the UI uses. Keyless: the model runs in the agent, not here.
mcp.orConfig: …or add to your agent's MCP config
mcp.capture: The tools include captureView — an agent can screenshot the app to see your rails (a tangled timeline, the coherence gantt), not just read the data.
mcp.fullGuide: Full guide — Store → Use with Claude (setup + examples) →
